observed_meaning: A temporary repository location that preserves pre-migration files for reference while canonical content is reorganized elsewhere.
semantic_consequence: Files in the staging location are evidence inputs, not the active authoring target or current contract owner.

observed_meaning: A staging location whose contents must remain unchanged after placement.
semantic_consequence: Later migration work may inspect the files but must not write corrections or canonical updates into that area.

observed_meaning: An independent review checkpoint that must be satisfied before the downstream migration Task may proceed.
semantic_consequence: Completion of the reviewed authoring work alone does not release the next Task; the review result and required sign-off control routing.

observed_meaning: Each review finding receives a disposition that either blocks the next Task until repaired or explicitly removes it from the immediate release boundary.
semantic_consequence: Unclassified findings cannot be ignored when deciding whether the downstream Task is executable.

observed_meaning: A review verdict that accepts the overall result while retaining bounded non-blocking findings.
semantic_consequence: The workflow may proceed after the named minor items are dispositioned, without treating the review as a clean finding-free pass.

observed_meaning: A migration rule that discards metadata-only provenance while retaining citations that were part of the source body.
semantic_consequence: Body citations remain authoritative migrated content, while removed front-matter dependencies do not have to be recreated elsewhere.

observed_meaning: A preserved copy whose evidentiary value depends on exact content equality with the source at the cutoff.
semantic_consequence: Any content difference would invalidate the snapshot as a faithful pre-migration baseline.

observed_meaning: Files explicitly excluded from the preservation operation even though they reside beside included files.
semantic_consequence: The Task must not copy or claim coverage for those assets, and later work cannot infer that they were part of the staged source set.

observed_meaning: A preserved baseline location that must not receive later edits.
semantic_consequence: Migration authoring must occur against active files rather than mutating the evidence snapshot.

observed_meaning: A contract subtype for APIs, tools, and external boundaries whose normative shape includes request, response, and error sections.
semantic_consequence: Only contracts in this class are required to use interface-oriented section structure.

observed_meaning: A contract subtype for document, table, metadata, and validation shapes that uses format-oriented normative sections.
semantic_consequence: These contracts must not be forced into request and response semantics that belong to interface contracts.

observed_meaning: Specification identity is derived from its repository location and maps one-to-one with that path.
semantic_consequence: Moving or renaming a Specification normally changes its canonical reference rather than preserving an identity independent of location.

observed_meaning: A Topics row identifies its child by canonical semantic reference rather than by physical file path.
semantic_consequence: Consumers must resolve the child through the canonical ref; the file column is not the authoritative relation field.
term_or_phrase: ref as canonical child target data

observed_meaning: Specification-local Source records sections are removed, and reverse traceability is governed by a separate ADR-backed policy.
semantic_consequence: A child Specification must not own ad hoc reverse-source lists that duplicate the canonical traceability model.
term_or_phrase: reverse traceability with ADR-governed traceability policy

observed_meaning: A path-derived identity mismatch is temporarily tolerated at warning severity in explicitly transitional states.
semantic_consequence: The same mismatch is an error for new or migrated stable Specifications, so lifecycle context changes validation outcome.
term_or_phrase: warning only during inventory, migration, or transient work

observed_meaning: The correction Task deliberately leaves deletion and Work Item closure to a later Task.
semantic_consequence: Satisfying the contract corrections does not authorize cleanup or lifecycle closure within this Task.

observed_meaning: Strict structural validation is a prerequisite gate before independent review begins.
semantic_consequence: The review route must not start while validator errors remain, even if migration authoring is otherwise complete.
term_or_phrase: before handing off to the Opus reviewer

observed_meaning: Within this migration gate, warnings emitted by strict mode are elevated to blocking failures.
semantic_consequence: A zero-error command exit is insufficient when strict-mode warnings remain; all diagnostics must be cleared before completion.
term_or_phrase: treat all --strict diagnostics as errors for migration completeness

observed_meaning: Verification scope is defined by the complete output directories rather than only the initially named index files.
semantic_consequence: Completion evidence must cover every migrated child file, preventing a partial validation claim based on a narrower command target.

observed_meaning: The PRODUCT authoring-standard artifact that owns current normative rules for Requirement records.
semantic_consequence: Requirement structure and author-facing behavior must be derived from this guide rather than duplicated in Task-local instructions.

observed_meaning: Metadata rules are separated by the lifecycle of an authoring operation rather than treated as one undifferentiated field set.
semantic_consequence: A field may be generated or prohibited at creation while still being required in the persisted record or allowed during update.
term_or_phrase: create, partial update, and persisted state

observed_meaning: Requirement source relations may point to multiple classes of active canonical references rather than only Requirements or Investigations.
semantic_consequence: Authors must not narrow source_refs to a Requirement-only provenance model.
term_or_phrase: canonical artifact IDs or active semantic refs

observed_meaning: The substantive body requirement for Required Outcome depends on the Requirement lifecycle state.
semantic_consequence: Draft or other non-accepted Requirements are not invalid solely because that section lacks accepted-state content, while accepted Requirements must provide it.
term_or_phrase: Required Outcome required only when status: accepted

observed_meaning: The root Specification directs content to top-level areas according to accepted semantic ownership.
semantic_consequence: New or migrated content must follow the router instead of choosing placement from physical convenience or historical location.

observed_meaning: The root router owns navigation and placement direction but not the detailed normative rules of its child areas.
semantic_consequence: Child contract text must remain in the child authority rather than being restated at the root.

observed_meaning: Each top-level area declares both the semantics it owns and the semantics it must not contain.
semantic_consequence: Placement decisions are governed by explicit positive and negative responsibility boundaries.

observed_meaning: The root index primarily routes readers and tools rather than serving as a detailed semantic contract.
semantic_consequence: Adding substantive child rules to the root would violate its intended responsibility.

observed_meaning: The PRODUCT BPDSL area temporarily preserves material without claiming current canonical BPDSL semantics.
semantic_consequence: Content in that area cannot be treated as authoritative BPDSL design and must eventually be removed, relocated, or redefined through its exit contract.
term_or_phrase: temporary non-canonical BPDSL quarantine and staging contract

observed_meaning: Repository-wide reference rewriting is intentionally reserved for a later Task despite completion of the top-level placement work.
semantic_consequence: This Task cannot claim global reference consistency or alter unrelated references as part of its close-out.

observed_meaning: Operational content removed from a generic PRODUCT contract is transferred to the application namespace that owns its concrete behavior.
semantic_consequence: The generic Specification stops being the authority for implementation-specific scanning, parsing, tool, UI, or projection behavior.

observed_meaning: DRMCP app-local Specifications consume generic PRODUCT authority by reference rather than duplicating its normative rules.
semantic_consequence: A DRMCP document must not become a competing authority for app-independent Design Records semantics.
term_or_phrase: reference PRODUCT-owned Design Records semantics instead of restating them

observed_meaning: The existing DRMCP Specification that already owns a concrete operational concern after the PRODUCT/DRMCP split.
semantic_consequence: When an adequate owner exists, the handoff retains that authority instead of creating a duplicate target.

observed_meaning: A disposition that keeps an already adequate app-local authority unchanged.
semantic_consequence: No new writer or contract is introduced for that concern, and absence of an edit does not mean the concern was omitted.

observed_meaning: A disposition that limits handoff authoring to the smallest correction needed for ownership consistency, such as replacing a stale semantic reference.
semantic_consequence: The Task must not use the handoff as authority for broader redesign or hierarchy expansion.

observed_meaning: A disposition that intentionally leaves a removed statement without an app-local replacement because no accepted contract requires one.
semantic_consequence: Deletion is considered complete only when the absence of a new owner is justified, not when the concern is silently dropped.

observed_meaning: An application Specification owns the explicit statement that a possible feature is outside the current MVP.
semantic_consequence: Preserving the exclusion documents non-activation; it does not create an implementation obligation or enable the feature.

observed_meaning: Formatting preservation applies only within the semantics of a named authoring operation, not to every byte of the file.
semantic_consequence: Consumers cannot infer that unrelated formatting or serialization is immutable across all update modes.

observed_meaning: Known mismatches are explicitly assigned to later owners rather than resolved inside the handoff Task.
semantic_consequence: Completion of this Task does not imply those gaps are fixed, and downstream work must preserve the named routing.

observed_meaning: Completed decision-ledger outcomes constrain the Investigation and are not reconsidered during conflict discovery.
semantic_consequence: The Investigation may identify projection conflicts but cannot adopt a different semantic choice from the accepted decisions.
term_or_phrase: treated as authority and were not reopened

observed_meaning: The Investigation records exact mismatches and owners while leaving resolution choices to a later decision phase.
semantic_consequence: A conflict entry is evidence for routing, not an accepted correction or canonical change.

observed_meaning: Each conflict is assigned to the workflow boundary responsible for deciding or implementing it.
semantic_consequence: A Task must not resolve conflicts owned by another Work Item, serialized writer phase, or downstream application authority.
term_or_phrase: declared owner: W016, W017, shared serialization, or downstream DRMCP

observed_meaning: A proposed scope for a later correction or decision that is recorded without adopting the disposition.
semantic_consequence: Downstream Tasks may use it as routing input, but it has no normative effect until the proper owner decides it.

observed_meaning: The accepted Specification or artifact that would own the corrected normative rule after downstream authoring.
semantic_consequence: The Investigation itself must not become the durable source of the current contract.

observed_meaning: Multiple Work Items that modify the same Specification are ordered so one writer completes before the next begins.
semantic_consequence: Concurrent writes to shared canonical files are prohibited, and integrated review follows the serialized writers.

observed_meaning: A decision Task may retain a short resumable reason while an ADR owns the durable rationale and alternatives.
semantic_consequence: Task Evidence can support workflow continuity without replacing ADR authority.
term_or_phrase: concise workflow rationale from canonical durable rationale

observed_meaning: Implementation, migration, and validator effects are acknowledged but assigned outside the current Work Item's decision boundary.
semantic_consequence: Their discovery does not authorize Specification or implementation changes in this Investigation Task.

observed_meaning: A conflict whose required semantic direction is already fixed by accepted authority and therefore needs no new user decision.
semantic_consequence: The downstream route may author the correction directly, but the Investigation itself still does not apply it.

observed_meaning: The completed decision authority resolves all material choices exposed by the Investigation.
semantic_consequence: A later decision Task must not reopen the accepted decisions merely because conflicts were found.

observed_meaning: PRODUCT fixes the semantic contract while parser, projection, indexing, and diagnostic mechanics remain assigned to DRMCP.
semantic_consequence: PRODUCT authoring must stop before choosing application implementation details, and DRMCP work must consume the accepted semantics later.

observed_meaning: A derived set of Work Items that directly cite a Requirement, distinct from broader graph traversal through intermediate records.
semantic_consequence: Reverse lookup must not be persisted reciprocally on the Requirement or conflated with transitive provenance traversal.

observed_meaning: A migration changes one record from the old provenance field shape to the new shape in one indivisible update.
semantic_consequence: The same record must not persist both old and new provenance metadata or an intermediate partially converted state.

observed_meaning: A migrated record uses either the legacy provenance fields or the accepted replacement contract, never both.
semantic_consequence: Mixed metadata is invalid even when repository-wide migration is staged across records.

observed_meaning: Specific workflow Tasks remain outside migration action because they bootstrap the transition under the old contract.
semantic_consequence: The exclusion is local to migration execution and must not become a general canonical exception to the new metadata rules.

observed_meaning: A conflict affects files written by multiple Work Items and therefore requires ordered, preservation-aware authoring.
semantic_consequence: The later writer may change only its owned relation wording and must preserve the earlier writer's accepted Task-type semantics.

observed_meaning: The source-relation writer must leave the previously accepted Task-type, single-responsibility, and design-state rules unchanged.
semantic_consequence: Shared-file access does not authorize re-deciding or weakening another Work Item's completed contract.

observed_meaning: The correction Task may act only on findings formally recorded by the named review Task.
semantic_consequence: The correction author cannot add unrelated improvements or expand scope from informal observations.

observed_meaning: Correction and independent determination that a finding is closed belong to separate Tasks.
semantic_consequence: The writer that repairs a finding cannot accept its own repair as closure Evidence.

observed_meaning: Only a predeclared bounded record set may be modified to repair the named findings.
semantic_consequence: Any additional required write invalidates the current correction route rather than silently widening it.

observed_meaning: Discovering that an unlisted target is unavoidable triggers a no-write blocked outcome.
semantic_consequence: The correction must be all within the accepted boundary or not begin; partial repair is prohibited.
term_or_phrase: Stop with BLOCKED without changing any record

observed_meaning: One review Task owns the authoritative cross-requirement verdict for the combined design state.
semantic_consequence: Parallel or duplicate review routes cannot produce competing acceptance authority.

observed_meaning: Closure readiness depends on the earlier review verdict and requires different Evidence for PASS versus NEEDS REVISION.
semantic_consequence: A direct PASS may release closure without correction Tasks, while a revision verdict requires completed correction and independent finding closure.

observed_meaning: Tasks that perform no real responsibility must not be executed merely to satisfy dependency metadata.
semantic_consequence: Conditional branches remain not required when unused, and release logic must consume the actual verdict instead of manufacturing completion records.

observed_meaning: Legacy bootstrap metadata is tolerated only for the specific transition workflow.
semantic_consequence: The exception must not be projected into the canonical metadata contract for ordinary Tasks.

observed_meaning: Each formal finding is linked to an exact set of correction artifacts and a required post-correction result.
semantic_consequence: Verification and re-review can reject changes that do not trace to a named finding or omit a required target.

observed_meaning: A reviewer separate from the correction author determines whether each repaired finding is closed.
semantic_consequence: Correction self-verification cannot substitute for the independent finding disposition required before closure.

observed_meaning: Evidence produced by the repair owner is informative but not authoritative for finding closure.
semantic_consequence: The workflow requires a separate review record even when the correction Task reports successful verification.
term_or_phrase: T09 self-verification was not accepted as independent closure Evidence

observed_meaning: Each reviewed finding receives one explicit terminal review disposition for the current re-review pass.
semantic_consequence: Open findings preserve blockers and correction targets; closed findings may release the next gate.

observed_meaning: The downstream closure Task is released only by a complete accepted review outcome or is stopped by a precisely recorded unresolved condition.
semantic_consequence: Ambiguous or partial re-review results cannot be used as closure authority.
term_or_phrase: accepted review result or an exact blocker

observed_meaning: All required finding dispositions are accepted as closed for the bounded re-review scope.
semantic_consequence: The named closure Tasks become ready, but this review does not itself perform lifecycle synchronization.

observed_meaning: A review-derived state indicating that downstream synchronization Tasks may begin.
semantic_consequence: Readiness is not the same as closure; Work Item and Task lifecycle changes remain owned by later Tasks.

observed_meaning: Finding closure review records acceptance Evidence without changing Work Item or Task lifecycle status.
semantic_consequence: Review authority and lifecycle synchronization remain separate responsibilities.
term_or_phrase: no lifecycle state was advanced by this Task

observed_meaning: ADR authorship follows previously selected decision boundaries rather than arbitrary file count or decision-row count.
semantic_consequence: Each durable choice set must be recorded exactly once in an ADR whose scope can change coherently.
term_or_phrase: one coherent ADR for each routed boundary

observed_meaning: The authoring Task translates fixed decision inputs into ADRs but does not reconsider the selected outcomes.
semantic_consequence: Any newly discovered unresolved choice must stop authoring and return to a decision owner.
term_or_phrase: Preserve accepted decisions without reopening them

observed_meaning: ADR boundaries must be neither so broad that independently changeable decisions are coupled nor so narrow that every ledger row becomes a separate record.
semantic_consequence: Boundary selection is based on coherent durable choice ownership, not document-size convenience.
term_or_phrase: Avoid both omnibus ADRs and one-row-per-ADR fragmentation

observed_meaning: Every routed decision boundary has one and only one ADR owner.
semantic_consequence: Duplicated or missing ADR coverage prevents completion.

observed_meaning: Accepted ADRs do not claim canonical Specification projection until the downstream synchronization Task completes.
semantic_consequence: ADR acceptance and migration-to-Specification status are separate lifecycle events.
term_or_phrase: migrated_to_spec remains null pending Specification synchronization

observed_meaning: Accepted workflow rules are projected into the specific Specifications that own their current normative form.
semantic_consequence: The authoring Task cannot choose alternative storage locations or leave the rules only in ADRs and Task Evidence.

observed_meaning: Each accepted rule is expressed as current contract text without being restated as competing authority across multiple Specifications.
semantic_consequence: Completion requires both full coverage and a single clear ownership location for each rule.

observed_meaning: A prior rule that required downstream progress to be written back into a completed decision Task is no longer valid.
semantic_consequence: Completed decision Tasks remain historical checkpoints and are not mutated to mirror ADR or Specification progress.

observed_meaning: Completed decision, authoring, and review records preserve the state that satisfied their own completion boundary.
semantic_consequence: Later Tasks own later status and references; prior records must not be reopened merely to show downstream completion.
term_or_phrase: historical Evidence without downstream progress writeback

observed_meaning: Correction and closure-review Tasks are created only after a review produces named findings.
semantic_consequence: A PASS route must not contain speculative no-op correction Tasks, and a revision route must separate repair from independent closure.
term_or_phrase: finding-driven conditional correction and independent finding-closure Task materialization

observed_meaning: Canonical writers that touch overlapping artifacts run in a deterministic order before a single review evaluates the combined state.
semantic_consequence: No writer may race another shared writer, and separate reviews cannot create competing final verdicts.
term_or_phrase: shared-writer serialization and one final integrated review

observed_meaning: Closure synchronization may only copy accepted state changes that follow directly from prior authority.
semantic_consequence: Any new judgment, graph change, or content decision stops synchronization and routes to its proper owner.
term_or_phrase: exact mechanically derivable lifecycle, Evidence, completion-result, and relation propagation

observed_meaning: A readiness check that must pass before substantive integrated review begins.
semantic_consequence: When a required owner, artifact, dependency, or Evidence source is missing, the reviewer stops without issuing semantic findings.

observed_meaning: A review result indicating that prerequisites for a valid verdict are not satisfied.
semantic_consequence: The review route must repair the missing prerequisites and later resume; NOT READY is not a semantic rejection of the combined design.

observed_meaning: A distinct investigation Task and durable Investigation artifact own bounded impact, conflict, uncertainty, and graph-change evidence.
semantic_consequence: ADR routing or authoring-time inspection cannot substitute for the required Investigation responsibility.

observed_meaning: Independent review relies on current artifacts and direct inspection rather than the reviewed author's completion claims.
semantic_consequence: Self-reported verification cannot establish review acceptance without independent evidence.
term_or_phrase: Author reports were not accepted as proof

observed_meaning: A single review Task owns the final acceptance result for the complete combined Work Item state.
semantic_consequence: The workflow avoids fragmented or competing final reviews across separately authored artifacts.

observed_meaning: Every material review issue must identify severity, affected decisions and artifacts, required outcome, judgment need, and owner type.
semantic_consequence: A vague concern cannot drive correction routing or block implementation planning.

observed_meaning: The review verdict explicitly withholds authorization to create production implementation work.
semantic_consequence: Implementation Task authoring remains blocked until the named design findings are repaired and independently closed.

observed_meaning: The downstream implementation-planning Task remains only a reserved branch until all required finding-closure reviews accept the repairs.
semantic_consequence: Correction completion alone cannot release implementation planning.
term_or_phrase: Do not materialize T08 until every closure-blocking finding is independently CLOSED

observed_meaning: The current workflow rule that determines whether an existing ADR may be amended or must be superseded.
semantic_consequence: A routing Task cannot select amend when the accepted authority classifies the change as a material ownership or architecture change.

observed_meaning: The first NOT READY review attempt remains in the completed Task as an immutable record alongside the later resumed verdict.
semantic_consequence: Reconvergence adds later Evidence without erasing the earlier prerequisite failure or pretending it never occurred.

observed_meaning: The coordination Task creates only the downstream responsibilities required by the named review findings.
semantic_consequence: The graph must mirror the finding types and dependencies without adding speculative work.

observed_meaning: Every materialized Task owns one distinct decision, authoring, correction, or review outcome.
semantic_consequence: Combining finding decision, repair, and closure into one Task would violate the graph contract.

observed_meaning: The implementation-planning branch remains unmaterialized while finding closure is pending.
semantic_consequence: A reserved identifier or conceptual next step is not an executable Task until the release condition is met.
term_or_phrase: Keep T08 reserved until T19 closes every required finding

observed_meaning: Coordination owns graph creation and dependency ordering but none of the child deliverables or judgments.
semantic_consequence: The coordination Task cannot satisfy or pre-empt the responsibilities it materializes.
term_or_phrase: This Task must not decide, author, repair, or review

observed_meaning: The Investigation owns a single research question about semantic checklist coverage, authority, and placement.
semantic_consequence: Unrelated validator design or checklist authoring cannot be absorbed into the same Investigation.

observed_meaning: Checklist semantics are partitioned into rules applying to every Task and rules applying only to one declared Task type.
semantic_consequence: A validator must compose both layers without duplicating common criteria in every type-specific checklist.

observed_meaning: Every proposed checklist topic must trace to a specific canonical Task-authoring rule.
semantic_consequence: No checklist criterion may be adopted solely from intuition or corpus frequency.

observed_meaning: The Investigation preserves unresolved facts and alternatives but does not convert them into accepted checklist rules.
semantic_consequence: A missing judgment must route to a decision owner before authoring proceeds.
term_or_phrase: Record uncertainty without selecting new design choices

observed_meaning: Every unresolved criterion, conflict, or graph candidate is assigned to the Task type responsible for resolving it.
semantic_consequence: Uncertainty cannot be left as an unowned note while downstream authoring claims readiness.

observed_meaning: The semantic checklist evaluates only the authored Task text and declared metadata, not unobserved repository or runtime facts.
semantic_consequence: External-state assertions require separate structural, execution, or review Evidence and cannot be manufactured by the semantic evaluator.
term_or_phrase: Task-local evaluation does not infer actual external artifact, graph, command, or reviewer state

observed_meaning: An internal model-output format is an implementation aid, not the public validation API.
semantic_consequence: Changing evaluator prompt structure does not by itself redefine the externally owned response schema.
term_or_phrase: evaluator-internal structured JSON instruction remains separate from any external validator response contract

observed_meaning: PRODUCT owns the app-independent meaning of Task responsibility validation.
semantic_consequence: Concrete application design must conform to these semantics but cannot redefine them locally.

observed_meaning: TRV owns interface, runtime, provider, packaging, tests, and other application-specific validator choices.
semantic_consequence: The PRODUCT Specification must delegate these concerns without choosing their implementation.
term_or_phrase: concrete app-local design to the TRV namespace

observed_meaning: Earlier implementation candidates remain provenance inputs rather than accepted current design.
semantic_consequence: TRV authoring cannot treat those choices as binding unless a TRV-local decision adopts them.

observed_meaning: The validator contract is defined independently of current DRMCP operation or embedding.
semantic_consequence: This Task cannot add DRMCP tool behavior or imply that integration already exists.

observed_meaning: The same semantic validator is invoked after Task authoring and again after successful completion Evidence is added.
semantic_consequence: A Task may pass initial authoring validation but still require a final semantic check before normal completion or release.

observed_meaning: When the validator reports a semantic violation, the surrounding workflow and human authority decide whether to accept or reject it.
semantic_consequence: The validator does not autonomously correct, complete, release, or overrule the Task.

observed_meaning: Coordination removes a resolved blocker so an already assigned writer may proceed.
semantic_consequence: The release Task does not replace the writer or author the checklist itself.
term_or_phrase: Release the existing W020 checklist authoring owner

observed_meaning: Exactly one Task owns modification of the checklist artifacts.
semantic_consequence: No duplicate writer may be materialized in the coordinating Work Item.

observed_meaning: A completed coordination Task is added as a prerequisite that proves the former semantic blocker has been resolved.
semantic_consequence: The existing authoring Task remains blocked until the canonical authority and release relation are present.

observed_meaning: The coordination Task may update dependencies and release order but not the checklist deliverable or review result.
semantic_consequence: Graph repair cannot absorb authoring, review, or implementation responsibility.
term_or_phrase: owns only graph and release changes

observed_meaning: The repaired Task graph contains a single authoritative checklist-writing Task.
semantic_consequence: Completion fails if another Task still claims the same output or authoring boundary.

observed_meaning: An unfinished Task may enter cancelled without cancelling its parent Work Item.
semantic_consequence: Task-level intentional abandonment is represented separately from abandonment of the parent outcome.

observed_meaning: A cancelled Task or Work Item cannot return to an active lifecycle state.
semantic_consequence: Materially resumed work requires a new record rather than reactivation of the cancelled record.

observed_meaning: Cancelling a Work Item cancels every owned unfinished Task while preserving owned done Tasks.
semantic_consequence: A cancelled Work Item is valid only after all owned Tasks are either done or cancelled.

observed_meaning: Cancelling one Task does not automatically change the parent Work Item status.
semantic_consequence: The parent may complete only if its current Completion Condition remains satisfied; otherwise a separate graph, condition, or cancellation change is required.
term_or_phrase: Parent Work Item after independent Task cancellation

observed_meaning: Cancellation is not treated as successful completion of a dependency.
semantic_consequence: Direct not-started dependents become blocked, and an already blocked dependent stays blocked.
term_or_phrase: A cancelled prerequisite does not satisfy depends_on

observed_meaning: Dependency failure blocks direct dependents but does not recursively cancel them.
semantic_consequence: Potentially recoverable Tasks remain available for later graph repair rather than being discarded.
term_or_phrase: No automatic cancellation propagates through Task dependencies

observed_meaning: The existing Evidence section records the stop reason, causal decision or change, and propagation results without new cancellation metadata.
semantic_consequence: Lifecycle meaning is documented substantively while avoiding another writable state surface.

observed_meaning: When a referenced child Work Item is cancelled, its work_item_execution Task is also cancelled.
semantic_consequence: The parent Work Item remains unchanged automatically, while dependents of the execution Task follow the cancelled-prerequisite rule.

observed_meaning: Only non-semantic repairs such as wording, references, factual Evidence, or mechanical relations are permitted after cancellation.
semantic_consequence: Any change to scope, procedure, outcome, or completion judgment must use a new Task or Work Item.

observed_meaning: A successor record may preserve provenance to cancelled work when that history directly informs the resumed effort.
semantic_consequence: The cancelled record remains historical Evidence but does not own the new completion boundary.
term_or_phrase: cites the cancelled record as a source when materially relevant

observed_meaning: A coordination phase converts completed decision and Investigation evidence into the exact downstream responsibility graph.
semantic_consequence: The route may be materialized only after the Investigation exposes the required owners and dependencies.

observed_meaning: Coordination materializes responsibilities proven necessary by accepted evidence and leaves unused conditional branches absent.
semantic_consequence: Speculative correction, review, or closure Tasks must not be created in advance.
term_or_phrase: Create only the required downstream Tasks

observed_meaning: Tasks that modify the same canonical artifacts are placed in a deterministic writer order.
semantic_consequence: Parallel execution is prohibited where outputs overlap, and the integrated review follows the final writer.

observed_meaning: The workflow first decides ADR coverage and disposition, then authors ADRs and Specifications from that fixed route.
semantic_consequence: Canonical authoring cannot choose its own ADR boundary or begin while routing remains unresolved.

observed_meaning: A single independent review evaluates the complete combined state after all serialized authoring is finished.
semantic_consequence: Partial pre-writer reviews cannot release closure or substitute for the final combined verdict.
term_or_phrase: one integrated independent review after the final writer

observed_meaning: Repair and closure-review branches remain conceptual rather than materialized before a review records actual findings.
semantic_consequence: A direct PASS route has no correction no-op Tasks, while a revision route is created from the named finding set.
term_or_phrase: correction and finding-closure review abstract until named findings exist

observed_meaning: Lifecycle closure cannot proceed without authoritative review Evidence and its required branch completion.
semantic_consequence: Authoring completion alone does not authorize Work Item closure.
term_or_phrase: Closure synchronization remains blocked until an accepted review route exists

observed_meaning: Each terminal decision receives one ADR-routing outcome describing whether new durable authority is needed, already exists, is unnecessary, or cannot proceed.
semantic_consequence: No decision may be omitted or assigned multiple incompatible routing outcomes.

observed_meaning: Each routed ADR boundary receives an explicit disposition for how durable authority will be represented.
semantic_consequence: Downstream authorship must follow the selected record operation rather than deciding it during writing.

observed_meaning: Durable choices are grouped into ADRs that share one changeable decision boundary without combining unrelated architecture concerns.
semantic_consequence: An ADR must neither absorb independently changeable choices nor fragment one coherent choice across records.

observed_meaning: Every amendment or supersession decision states whether the new choice changes the existing architecture or ownership boundary materially.
semantic_consequence: A material reversal cannot be hidden as an in-place amendment, while compatible extension need not create false supersession history.

observed_meaning: ADR evolution must accurately show whether prior authority remains valid, is extended, or has been replaced.
semantic_consequence: Record disposition cannot be chosen merely for editing convenience.

observed_meaning: Cancellation first fixes the complete set of records whose lifecycle must change and then writes the whole transition as one operation.
semantic_consequence: Partial propagation that leaves an incoherent Work Item and Task state is prohibited.
term_or_phrase: atomic affected-set computation and all-or-nothing propagation

observed_meaning: The second semantic validator checkpoint applies before done finalization, not before cancellation.
semantic_consequence: Cancellation readiness is governed by lifecycle and Evidence rules rather than a completion-oriented semantic validation result.

observed_meaning: ADR authoring and canonical/workflow-support authoring complete before one reviewer judges the combined result.
semantic_consequence: Neither authoring boundary may self-accept or release closure independently.
term_or_phrase: One independent review Task after both authoring boundaries

observed_meaning: A direct closure owner can be created once its PASS dependency and exact writable closure targets are known.
semantic_consequence: The synchronization Task remains limited to accepted lifecycle closure and cannot implement cancellation mechanics or modify unrelated records.
term_or_phrase: One synchronization Task may be materialized after the integrated review Task

observed_meaning: The Task ended intentionally without performing its primary outcome.
semantic_consequence: Its Evidence records the replacement route, and no partial extraction result may be attributed to it.

observed_meaning: Parallel sessions would have written into the same Task Evidence section, violating one-writer ownership.
semantic_consequence: The original Task cannot safely execute in parallel and must be replaced by independently owned outputs.

observed_meaning: Replacement Tasks use disjoint corpus scopes and separate Evidence write targets.
semantic_consequence: They may execute concurrently without file-level write conflicts.

observed_meaning: The downstream reconciliation Task's prerequisites are changed from the cancelled Task to all successor Tasks.
semantic_consequence: The cancelled prerequisite does not leave the dependent blocked because the graph repair occurs in the same coordination route.
term_or_phrase: re-pointed to depend on the five replacement Tasks

observed_meaning: One Task with a common Evidence target is replaced by multiple Tasks with independent write ownership.
semantic_consequence: The workflow graph changes to permit safe parallel execution without changing the overall corpus outcome.

observed_meaning: Each replacement Investigation Task owns a distinct, non-overlapping source partition.
semantic_consequence: No source or output is jointly authored by parallel Tasks, while the union preserves the original scope.

observed_meaning: Cancellation of the old prerequisite and re-pointing of its dependent occur as one coherent graph update.
semantic_consequence: The directly dependent Task is never left in an intermediate invalid or blocked state caused only by the repair operation.

observed_meaning: Writer ownership is exclusive at the file or section target used by each parallel Task.
semantic_consequence: Parallel safety is not established merely by disjoint reading scope; write targets must also be disjoint.
term_or_phrase: no two Tasks write to the same Evidence target

observed_meaning: The coordination Task changes the graph but does not perform the Investigation deliverable owned by its child Tasks.
semantic_consequence: Graph repair cannot be counted as source extraction or artifact authoring completion.

observed_meaning: The source set is frozen at the observed cutoff before extraction begins.
semantic_consequence: Later status changes or newly created Tasks do not silently alter the completion count for this extraction Task.
term_or_phrase: Fix this Task's corpus at start

observed_meaning: When legacy Tasks lack declared task_type metadata, their responsibility grouping is derived from title, Work, and Done Condition.
semantic_consequence: Missing modern metadata does not remove a source from coverage, but the inferred classification must remain distinct from an explicit declaration.

observed_meaning: Every source is scanned, but a source may legitimately produce zero vocabulary observations.
semantic_consequence: Coverage accountability is separate from candidate count, preventing fabricated findings to satisfy apparent productivity.

observed_meaning: Responsibility clusters label observed phrases but do not create additional Task or corpus partitions.
semantic_consequence: Classification does not change writer ownership or the assigned source boundary.
term_or_phrase: classification target for findings, not a further split axis

observed_meaning: A bounded Investigation result may be stored directly in the Task Evidence instead of a separate Investigation record because the user judged a formal record disproportionate.
semantic_consequence: The Task must record that judgment and still depend on a downstream Task that concludes or projects the result.

observed_meaning: A later Task must verify, reconcile, project, or explicitly reject further action on the lightweight Investigation result.
semantic_consequence: Direct Task Evidence is not allowed to become an unconsumed terminal research artifact.

observed_meaning: The vocabulary target column describes the responsibility represented by a phrase without approving preferred wording.
semantic_consequence: The extraction log remains observational evidence and cannot be used as a term-definition authority.
term_or_phrase: does not select a canonical term

observed_meaning: Completion requires preserving observed wording without normalizing or choosing a preferred vocabulary.
semantic_consequence: Any definition or approval work belongs to a separate downstream decision or authoring boundary.
term_or_phrase: no canonical term decision was made

observed_meaning: The complete previously collected observation tables are the source authority for reorganization, not only the subset promoted as boundary violations.
semantic_consequence: The reference must preserve ordinary in-type phrasing that a boundary-only artifact intentionally excludes.

observed_meaning: An observational artifact groups real corpus phrasing by Task responsibility type without defining preferred terminology.
semantic_consequence: The artifact documents usage breadth but does not validate correctness or replace canonical Task-type semantics.

observed_meaning: Normal per-type phrasing and cross-type disguise patterns have distinct artifact responsibilities.
semantic_consequence: Changes to the general reference must not alter the boundary-violation guide or blur their different selection criteria.

observed_meaning: The author records a bounded procedural deviation because the required source-type metadata was unavailable without violating the no-re-read boundary.
semantic_consequence: Consumers can distinguish the actual grouping method from the intended method and must not treat them as identical.
term_or_phrase: pragmatic substitution, not the literal instruction as written

observed_meaning: The derived reference deduplicates repeated phrasing for readability while the raw logs retain occurrence-level evidence.
semantic_consequence: Frequency or exhaustive occurrence claims must use the source logs, not the deduplicated projection.
term_or_phrase: source logs remain the frequency-accurate record

observed_meaning: The inventory corpus is defined by explicit repository path inclusions and exclusions rather than by a prior semantic classification of Design Records.
semantic_consequence: Manifest construction must enumerate the accepted paths mechanically and must not broaden scope from artifact interpretation.

observed_meaning: Manifest hashes and metadata capture a useful point-in-time view while accepting concurrent source changes.
semantic_consequence: Snapshot drift is diagnostic and must not be mistaken for a guarantee that source files remained unchanged during parallel extraction.
term_or_phrase: best-effort snapshots rather than immutable authority

observed_meaning: PRODUCT-INV-SPEC-011 owns the research method, narrative, and concluded facts for the corpus inventory.
semantic_consequence: Batch data files are machine-readable Evidence and do not replace the Investigation as the durable research artifact.

observed_meaning: The batch assignment file is the authoritative enumeration of each extraction Task's source scope.
semantic_consequence: Task prose cannot add, remove, or override assigned files, preventing divergence between graph description and executable scope.
term_or_phrase: exact source files come from the persisted batch JSON files, not prose duplication in Task records

observed_meaning: Each observations JSONL and coverage JSON file is assigned to exactly one extraction Task.
semantic_consequence: Parallel Tasks must not write another batch's outputs or share result files.

observed_meaning: A source hash or snapshot mismatch is recorded but is non-blocking when the source remains readable and dispositioned.
semantic_consequence: Structural completion may pass despite drift, while the coverage output still exposes the changed snapshot state.

observed_meaning: Creating the Investigation shell or completing individual batches does not conclude the research lifecycle.

term_or_phrase: Investigation remains investigating until all batches and final coverage reconciliation complete

observed_meaning: The Work Item deliberately retains independent batch result files without a combined observations artifact.
semantic_consequence: Completion and downstream consumers must use the batch set and coverage reconciliation rather than expecting a single merged writer target.
term_or_phrase: Do not create a merged master JSONL

observed_meaning: Tool implementation, Investigation-shell authoring, graph materialization, extraction, validation, and closure are assigned to separate Tasks.
semantic_consequence: No Task may claim another phase's outcome merely because the phases belong to one Work Item.

observed_meaning: Generated records from the current inventory workflow are excluded from the corpus to avoid observing artifacts created by the extraction process itself.
semantic_consequence: The manifest must retain only the pre-snapshot planning records explicitly accepted and exclude later T03–T38 records and the Investigation shell.
term_or_phrase: must not become self-observing inventory sources
